### 4. KEY MULTI-OS INSTALLATION PATTERNS

#### **Pattern A: Homebrew on macOS, apt on Linux**

Example from `base` role:
```yaml
# macOS - Homebrew
- name: Install base packages (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name: [git, curl, wget, ripgrep, fd, jq, tree, just]

# Linux - apt
- name: Install base packages (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: [git, curl, wget, ripgrep, fd-find, jq, tree, build-essential]
    update_cache: true
    cache_valid_time: 3600

# Note: fd-find → symlink as fd on Debian/Ubuntu
- name: Create fd symlink on Debian/Ubuntu
  ansible.builtin.file:
    src: /usr/bin/fdfind
    dest: /usr/bin/fd
    state: link
```

#### **Pattern B: GitHub Release Download with Architecture Mapping**

Used by ~20 roles (devtools, networking_tools, security_tools, iac_tools, etc.)

Example from `devtools` (gh installation):
```yaml
- name: Check if gh is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  command: gh --version
  register: gh_check

- name: Set gh release architecture
  set_fact:
    gh_release_arch: >-
      {{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
         else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
         else '' }}

# System-level install with sudo
- name: Install gh from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - gh_check.rc != 0
    - gh_release_arch != ''
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  block:
    - name: Get latest gh release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/releases/latest
      register: gh_release
    
    - name: Download gh .deb package
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/{{ gh_release.json.tag_name }}/gh_{{ ... }}_linux_{{ gh_release_arch }}.deb"
        dest: /tmp/gh.deb
    
    - name: Install gh .deb
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        deb: /tmp/gh.deb

# User-level fallback (no sudo)
- name: Install gh from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - gh_recheck.rc != 0
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
    
    - name: Download & extract gh tarball
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "...gh_{{ ... }}_linux_{{ gh_release_arch }}.tar.gz"
        dest: /tmp/gh.tar.gz
    
    - name: Extract & install
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        tar -xzf /tmp/gh.tar.gz -C /tmp/gh-extract
        gh_bin="$(find /tmp/gh-extract -path '*/bin/gh' | head -n1)"
        install -m 0755 "$gh_bin" "$HOME/.local/bin/gh"
```

**Key Features:**
- System-level install with `become: true` (via apt/deb)
- Fallback to user-level (`~/.local/bin`) if sudo fails
- Retries: 3 attempts with 5s delay for network resilience
- Architecture mapping: x86_64/amd64 → amd64, aarch64/arm64 → arm64
- Cleanup: removes temp files in rescue block

#### **Pattern C: Language-Specific Package Managers (uv, cargo, gem)**

Example from `security_tools` (pre-commit via uv):
```yaml
- name: Install pre-commit via uv (pinned Python 3.13, all OSes)
  ansible.builtin.command: uv tool install --force pre-commit --python 3.13
  changed_when: "'already installed' not in output"
```

Example from `python_uv_tools`:
```yaml
- name: Install Python CLI tools via uv
  command: >-
    uv tool install {{ item.name }}
    {% if item.python %}--python {{ item.python }}{% endif %}
    {% if item.with %}{% for dep in item.with %}--with {{ dep }}{% endfor %}{% endif %}
  args:
    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.binary }}"
  environment:
    UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT: "120"
    UV_HTTP_RETRIES: "5"
  when: not (item.needs_modern_gcc and gcc_too_old)
  loop: "{{ python_uv_tools }}"
```

#### **Pattern D: Conditional Installation with Defaults**

Example from `iac_tools`:
```yaml
# defaults/main.yml
iac_install_azure_cli: true
iac_install_terraform: true
iac_install_opentofu: true

# tasks/main.yml
- name: Install Azure CLI (macOS)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
    - iac_install_azure_cli
  block:
    - name: Install azure-cli via Homebrew
      community.general.homebrew:
        name: azure-cli
      register: az_brew_install
      until: az_brew_install is succeeded
      retries: 3
      delay: 20
  rescue:
    - name: Warn Azure CLI failed
      debug:
        msg: "Azure CLI installation failed — skipping."
```

#### **Pattern E: RedHat/CentOS Support with yum CLI**

Used in `base`, `networking_tools`, `iac_tools` roles:
```yaml
- name: Install base packages (RedHat/CentOS) — yum CLI for CentOS 7 compat
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
  become: true
  shell: |
    set -e
    missing=()
    for p in git curl wget jq tree gcc; do
      rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
    done
    if [ -z "${missing[*]:-}" ]; then
      echo "ALL_INSTALLED"
      exit 0
    fi
    yum install -y "${missing[@]}"
  changed_when: "'ALL_INSTALLED' not in output"
```

**Why yum CLI instead of ansible.builtin.yum?**
- ansible-core 2.18+ routes yum through dnf backend
- CentOS 7 has no dnf binary → breaks
- `yum` CLI works on CentOS 7, Rocky 8+, Alma 8+ (see `pitfalls/centos7-ansible-yum-dnf-backend.md`)

#### **Pattern F: CentOS 7 GCC Version Detection**

From `python_uv_tools`:
```yaml
- name: Detect host C compiler (gcc) version
  shell: gcc -dumpversion 2>/dev/null | head -1 || echo "0"
  register: gcc_version_probe

- name: Set fact gcc_too_old
  set_fact:
    gcc_too_old: "{{ ((gcc_version_probe.stdout | trim).split('.')[0] | int) < 9 }}"

# Skip numpy 2.x / pandas 3.x builds on CentOS 7 (gcc 4.8.5)
when: not (item.needs_modern_gcc and gcc_too_old)
```

### 5. CHEZMOI INTEGRATION & BREWFILE EXECUTION

**Location:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`

**When it runs:**
- Triggered when any Brewfile changes (chezmoi run_onchange)
- Only if `installBrewApps: true` or macOS + `installAiDesktopApps: true`

**How it works:**
```bash
# Detects Homebrew path (Intel vs Apple Silicon, macOS vs Linuxbrew)
if [[ -f /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
fi

# Runs shared Brewfile first (installs mas, taps)
run_bundle_with_retry "$BREWFILE_DIR/Brewfile" "shared packages"

# Runs platform-specific file
if [[ eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" ]]; then
    run_bundle_with_retry "$BREWFILE_DIR/Brewfile.darwin" "macOS packages"
else
    run_bundle_with_retry "$BREWFILE_DIR/Brewfile.linux" "Linux packages"
fi

# Retries with BUNDLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2 (default)
run_bundle_with_retry() {
    local file="$1"
    for attempt in 1 .. N; do
        if brew bundle --file="$file" --no-upgrade; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
}
```

**Architecture Support:**
- macOS: Detects `/opt/homebrew` (Apple Silicon) vs `/usr/local` (Intel)
- Linux: Detects `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew` vs `$HOME/.linuxbrew`
- Sudo handling: Pre-authenticates for macOS cask installers (e.g., google-drive, ollama-app)

### 10. ERROR HANDLING & RESILIENCE

**Patterns used:**

1. **Retries with exponential backoff:**
   ```yaml
   retries: 3
   delay: 5
   until: result is succeeded
   ```

2. **Network timeout protection:**
   ```yaml
   environment:
     UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT: "120"
     UV_HTTP_RETRIES: "5"
   timeout: 120
   ```

3. **Block + rescue for graceful degradation:**
   ```yaml
   block:
     - name: System-level install
   rescue:
     - name: Warn and clean up
       debug: msg "Installation failed — skipping"
     - name: Clean temp files
   ```

4. **Ignore errors on optional installs:**
   ```yaml
   ignore_errors: true  # (for non-critical tools)
   ```

5. **Brew bundle retry with partial success:**
   ```bash
   # Retries up to N times; subsequent runs only retry failed items
   brew bundle --no-upgrade
   ```

### Profile Values and Configuration

The dotfiles repo uses a templated approach with Chezmoi. The core configuration file is `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` which exposes:

**Available Profiles:**
- `macos` (default on macOS)
- `ubuntu_desktop` (Linux with GUI)
- `ubuntu_server` (Linux headless)
- `centos_server` (CentOS/Rocky/Alma)

**Feature Flags (all prompted once at init, stored in `.chezmoi.toml`):**
- `installCodingAgents` (Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, etc.) - default `true`
- `installBitwarden` (+ CLI, SSH Agent, Desktop on desktop profiles) - default `false`
- `installPythonUvTools` (mlflow, sqlit-tui, tmuxp, etc.) - default `true`
- `installJsCliTools` (readability-cli for web reader, etc.) - default `true`
- `installNetworkingTools` (nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy, etc.) - default `false`
- `installLlmTools` (Ollama, LiteLLM, llmfit, models) - default `false`
- `installIacTools` (Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu) - default `false`
- `installMediaTools` (ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips) - default `false`
- `installDotnetTools` (.NET SDK via mise, dotnet global tools) - default `false`
- `installAiDesktopApps` (Claude, ChatGPT, OpenCode, Codex, Ollama app) - macOS only, default `false`
- `installBrewApps` (general GUI apps) - default `false`
- `installInputMethod` (McBopomofo, RIME) - default `false`
- `useChineseMirror` (GFW mirrors) - default `false`
- `noRoot` (user-only, no sudo) - default `false`
- `discordChannel` (flatpak|deb|none, ubuntu_desktop only) - default `flatpak`
- `primaryShell` (zsh|bash) - default `zsh`
- `allowPartialFailure` (continue if one Ansible role fails) - default `false`
- `motdStyle` (figlet|fastfetch-slim|fastfetch-full) - default `figlet`
- `backupMode` (smart|full|off) - default `smart`
- `gitleaksAllRepos` (enable gitleaks for all repos) - default `false`

87	#   - fastfetch-slim: figlet hostname + fastfetch 精簡版（~10 行，~80ms）
88	#   - fastfetch-full: fastfetch 完整輸出含 distro logo（~22 行，~150ms）
89	# Runtime override: 在 ~/.zshrc.adhoc 設 MOTD_STYLE=... 可即時切換無需 chezmoi init --force
90	motdStyle = {{ promptChoiceOnce . "motdStyle" "SSH login banner style (figlet|fastfetch-slim|fastfetch-full)" (list "figlet" "fastfetch-slim" "fastfetch-full") "figlet" | quote }}
91	# Primary interactive shell — decides which shell `chsh` switches to as the
92	# login shell. Both ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc are deployed regardless (so the
93	# other shell still works ad-hoc); only the login-shell switch is gated.
94	# Bash side ships with oh-my-bash + ble.sh for a UX close to zsh; on macOS
95	# the bash role also brew-installs bash 5.x (system bash 3.2 is too old for
96	# OMB plugins) when bash is selected. See docs/shells/bash.md.
97	primaryShell = {{ promptChoiceOnce . "primaryShell" "Primary interactive shell (zsh|bash)" (list "zsh" "bash") "zsh" | quote }}
98	
99	# https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/use-scripts-to-perform-actions/#dont-show-scripts-that-would-run-in-chezmoi-diffchezmoi-status
100	[diff]
101	    exclude = ["scripts"]
102	{{- if lookPath "delta" }}
103	    # Side-by-side diff: left = current (before apply), right = target (after apply)
104	    pager = "delta --side-by-side --line-numbers --navigate --paging=always --file-style=yellow --file-decoration-style='yellow ul' --hunk-header-decoration-style='blue box'"
105	{{- end }}
106	[status]
107	    exclude = ["scripts"]
108

12	    # Note: set_fact cannot reliably override ansible_facts['architecture']
13	    # when inject_facts_as_vars=False, so we use a dedicated variable instead.

16	      register: dpkg_arch_result
17	      changed_when: false
18	      failed_when: false
19	      tags: [always]

22	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
23	        target_architecture: >-
24	          {{ {'amd64': 'x86_64', 'arm64': 'aarch64', 'armhf': 'armv7l', 'armel': 'armv6l', 'i386': 'i686'}
25	             [dpkg_arch_result.stdout | trim]
26	             | default(ansible_facts['architecture']) }}
27	      when: dpkg_arch_result.rc == 0 and dpkg_arch_result.stdout | trim != ''
28	      tags: [always]

30	    - name: Fallback target_architecture to gathered facts
31	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
32	        target_architecture: "{{ ansible_facts['architecture'] }}"
33	      when: target_architecture is not defined

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# upgrade_tools.sh — explicit, opt-in upgrade entrypoint.

4	# `chezmoi apply` is deliberately conservative (install-only, `state: present`,

6	# (or `just upgrade-*`) when you want to actually move tools forward.
7	#
8	# Design: each category is best-effort. A failure in one category does NOT
9	# abort later categories; a summary is printed at the end listing SUCCESS /
10	# FAILED / SKIPPED categories.
11	#
12	# Usage:
13	#   scripts/upgrade_tools.sh [all|<category> ...] [flags]
14	#
15	# Categories (also selectable via `all`):
16	#   externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem agents plugins
17	#

19	#   --dry-run          Print commands without executing.
20	#   --only a,b,c       Only run listed categories (comma-separated).
21	#   --skip a,b         Run everything except listed categories.

46	warn() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_YLW}[WARN]${_C_RST} $*"; }

199	_run() {

354	  fi

356	  info "Upgrading installed mise tools"
357	  _run "$mise_bin" upgrade || any_fail=1
358	
359	  return "$any_fail"

456	# ============================================================================
457	# Category: dotnet — upgrade each tool in dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml
458	# ============================================================================
459	cat_dotnet() {
460	  # Resolve dotnet via mise shim first, then system PATH.
461	  local dotnet_cmd=""
462	  if [[ -x "$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/dotnet" ]]; then
463	    dotnet_cmd="$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/dotnet"
464	  elif command -v dotnet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
465	    dotnet_cmd="dotnet"
466	  else
467	    warn "dotnet not found — skipping"
468	    return $SKIP_RC
469	  fi
470	
471	  # Parse the tools list from defaults YAML. Small hand-rolled parser: we
472	  # only need lines of the form `  - name: <pkg>`. If parsing produces no
473	  # results, fall back to `dotnet tool list --global`.
474	  local defaults_file="$_REPO_ROOT/dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml"
475	  local tools=()
476	  if [[ -f "$defaults_file" ]]; then
477	    while IFS= read -r line; do
478	      tools+=("$line")
479	    done < <(awk '
480	            /^dotnet_tools:/ { in_list=1; next }
481	            in_list && /^[^ ]/ { in_list=0 }
482	            in_list && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:/ {
483	                sub(/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:[[:space:]]*/, "")
484	                gsub(/["'"'"']/, "")
485	                print
486	            }
487	        ' "$defaults_file")
488	  fi
489	
490	  if [[ ${#tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
491	    info "Falling back to 'dotnet tool list --global'"
492	    if ! mapfile -t tools < <("$dotnet_cmd" tool list --global 2>/dev/null \
493	      | awk 'NR>2 && NF>0 {print $1}'); then
494	      warn "could not enumerate dotnet tools"
495	      return $SKIP_RC
496	    fi
497	  fi
498	
499	  if [[ ${#tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
500	    warn "no dotnet tools to upgrade — skipping"
501	    return $SKIP_RC
502	  fi
503	
504	  # dotnet tools land under ~/.dotnet/tools.
505	  export PATH="$HOME/.dotnet/tools:$PATH"
506	
507	  local any_fail=0
508	  for t in "${tools[@]}"; do
509	    info "Upgrading dotnet tool: $t"
510	    _run "$dotnet_cmd" tool update --global "$t" || any_fail=1
511	  done
512	  return "$any_fail"
513	}

537	# ============================================================================
538	# Category: flatpak — `flatpak update` for user-scope Flathub apps
539	# ============================================================================
540	# We deliberately stick to user-scope (`--user`): no sudo required, and our
541	# ansible role installs everything via `method: user`. System-scope flatpaks
542	# need `sudo flatpak update --system`, which the user can run manually if
543	# they have any (rare in this repo's flow).
544	cat_flatpak() {
545	  if ! command -v flatpak >/dev/null 2>&1; then
546	    warn "flatpak not installed — skipping"
547	    return $SKIP_RC
548	  fi
549	
550	  # Skip silently when there's nothing user-scoped to update — avoids logging
551	  # a "Nothing to do." into upgrade summaries on machines that have never set
552	  # discordChannel=flatpak.
553	  local n_user_apps
554	  n_user_apps="$(flatpak list --app --user 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
555	  if [[ "$n_user_apps" -eq 0 ]]; then
556	    info "No user-scope Flatpak apps installed — skipping"
557	    return $SKIP_RC
558	  fi
559	
560	  local any_fail=0
561	  info "Upgrading user-scope Flatpak apps ($n_user_apps installed)"
562	  _run flatpak update --user --noninteractive --assumeyes || any_fail=1
563	  return "$any_fail"
564	}

566	# ============================================================================
567	# Category: warp — Linux apt-only upgrade for Warp Terminal
568	# ============================================================================
569	# macOS Warp is handled by `cat_brew` (cask "warp" + --greedy). On Linux,
570	# Warp's only supported channel is its own apt repo, but the in-app updater
571	# pastes `... && warp_finish_update <token>` into the prompt — that token is
572	# only valid inside a live Warp session and `warp_finish_update` is a
573	# Warp-injected shell function (not on PATH otherwise). So this category
574	# does the apt half only and leaves the user to restart Warp themselves.
575	#
576	# See docs/tools/warp.md for the full mechanism (token IPC handshake, etc.).
577	cat_warp() {
578	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Linux" ]]; then
579	    info "Not Linux — Warp is upgraded via brew cask, skipping"
580	    return $SKIP_RC
581	  fi
582	  if ! command -v warp-terminal >/dev/null 2>&1; then
583	    warn "warp-terminal not installed — skipping"
584	    return $SKIP_RC
585	  fi
586	
587	  # warp-terminal is gated behind sudo apt. Reuse the shared sudo session so
588	  # the user isn't re-prompted across upgrade categories.
589	  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]] && declare -F sudo_session_init >/dev/null 2>&1; then
590	    if ! sudo_session_init "upgrade-warp"; then
591	      warn "Sudo session could not be established — skipping"
592	      return $SKIP_RC
593	    fi
594	    case "$(sudo_session_skip_reason)" in
595	      non-interactive | "")
596	        warn "Non-interactive mode without passwordless sudo — skipping warp"
597	        return $SKIP_RC
598	        ;;
599	    esac
600	  fi
601	
602	  local any_fail=0
603	  info "Refreshing Warp apt repo + installing only the warp-terminal candidate"
604	  # `apt update` covers all repos (cheap; usually run once per session anyway).
605	  _run sudo apt-get update || any_fail=1
606	  # `--only-upgrade` ensures we never accidentally re-install if the package
607	  # was uninstalled between commands; `-y` is safe because we're pinned to
608	  # one package name.
609	  _run sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y warp-terminal || any_fail=1
610	
611	  if [[ "$any_fail" -eq 0 ]]; then
612	    info "Warp on-disk binary updated. Quit + relaunch Warp to load the new version."
613	    info "(The in-app 'warp_finish_update <token>' graceful-restart only works from inside Warp.)"
614	  fi
615	  return "$any_fail"
616	}

618	# ============================================================================
619	# Category: agents — re-run install.sh for curl-installed CLI tools
620	# ============================================================================
621	# Only re-runs when the binary is already present. The installers are (by
622	# design) idempotent self-upgrades.
623	cat_agents() {
624	  local any_fail=0
625	  local ran_any=0
626	
627	  # Strategy: prefer the binary's built-in self-update subcommand (fast no-op
628	  # when already current; doesn't re-download the full binary). Fallback to
629	  # the official curl installer if the subcommand fails, hangs, or doesn't
630	  # exist. Inspection of upstream installers (2026-04) confirmed none of them
631	  # delegate to the self-update subcommand internally:
632	  #   - claude.sh   : always re-downloads, no version check
633	  #   - opencode.sh : has a same-version fast-path, but no `opencode upgrade`
634	  #   - cursor.sh   : always re-downloads, no version check
635	  #
636	  # We wrap the self-update call with a timeout (some `claude update` runs
637	  # have been observed hanging indefinitely on network checks) so a stuck
638	  # subcommand cannot block the whole upgrade flow.
639	  local _timeout_bin=""
640	  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
641	    _timeout_bin="timeout"
642	  elif command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
643	    _timeout_bin="gtimeout"
644	  fi
645	  _try_self_update_then_curl() {
646	    local label="$1" self_cmd="$2" curl_url="$3"
647	    info "Upgrading $label (trying self-update first)"
648	    local wrapped="$self_cmd"
649	    if [[ -n "$_timeout_bin" ]]; then
650	      wrapped="$_timeout_bin 90 $self_cmd"
651	    fi
652	    if _run_sh "$wrapped"; then
653	      return 0
654	    fi
655	    warn "$label self-update failed/timed out — falling back to official installer"
656	    local fallback="curl -fsSL $curl_url | bash"
657	    if [[ -n "$_timeout_bin" ]]; then
658	      fallback="$_timeout_bin 300 bash -c 'curl -fsSL $curl_url | bash'"
659	    fi
660	    _run_sh "$fallback"
661	  }
662	
663	  # Claude Code — `claude update` (alias: `claude upgrade`)
664	  if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 \
665	    || [[ -x "$HOME/.claude/local/bin/claude" ]]; then
666	    _try_self_update_then_curl "Claude Code" \
667	      "claude update" \
668	      "https://claude.ai/install.sh" || any_fail=1
669	    ran_any=1
670	  fi
671	
672	  # OpenCode — `opencode upgrade`
673	  if command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
674	    _try_self_update_then_curl "OpenCode" \
675	      "opencode upgrade" \
676	      "https://opencode.ai/install" || any_fail=1
677	    ran_any=1
678	  fi
679	
680	  # Cursor CLI — `cursor-agent update`
681	  if command -v cursor-agent >/dev/null 2>&1 \
682	    || command -v cursor-cli >/dev/null 2>&1 \
683	    || [[ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/cursor-agent" ]]; then
684	    _try_self_update_then_curl "Cursor CLI" \
685	      "cursor-agent update" \
686	      "https://cursor.com/install" || any_fail=1
687	    ran_any=1
688	  fi
689	
690	  # Ollama — Linux official installer (macOS is Homebrew-managed elsewhere).
691	  # No self-update subcommand exists.
692	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Linux" ]] && command -v ollama >/dev/null 2>&1; then
693	    info "Upgrading Ollama (Linux installer)"
694	    _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh" || any_fail=1
695	    ran_any=1
696	  fi
697	
698	  # llmfit — official local installer (Linux; macOS uses Homebrew)
699	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Linux" ]] && command -v llmfit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
700	    info "Upgrading llmfit (Linux local installer)"
701	    _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://llmfit.axjns.dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --local" || any_fail=1
702	    ran_any=1
703	  fi
704	
705	  # RTK — official installer (no self-update subcommand)
706	  if command -v rtk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
707	    info "Upgrading RTK"
708	    _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh" || any_fail=1
709	    ran_any=1
710	  fi
711	
712	  # SpecStory — brew tap when available (macOS), else GitHub release script.
713	  # The installer script is idempotent and pulls latest by default, so re-running
714	  # it is the upgrade path on Linux (and on macOS when not brew-managed).
715	  if command -v specstory >/dev/null 2>&1 \
716	    || [[ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/specstory" ]]; then
717	    local specstory_handled=0
718	    if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Darwin" ]] && setup_brew_path \
719	      && brew list --formula specstoryai/tap/specstory >/dev/null 2>&1; then
720	      info "Upgrading SpecStory via Homebrew tap"
721	      _run brew upgrade specstoryai/tap/specstory || any_fail=1
722	      specstory_handled=1
723	    fi
724	    if [[ "$specstory_handled" -eq 0 ]]; then
725	      if [[ -x "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/install_specstory.sh" ]]; then
726	        info "Upgrading SpecStory via install_specstory.sh (latest GitHub release)"
727	        _run "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/install_specstory.sh" || any_fail=1
728	      else
729	        warn "specstory present but install_specstory.sh not found — skipping"
730	      fi
731	    fi
732	    ran_any=1
733	  fi
734	
735	  if [[ "$ran_any" -eq 0 ]]; then
736	    warn "no known curl-installed agents detected — skipping"
737	    return $SKIP_RC
738	  fi
739	
740	  return "$any_fail"
741	}

743	# ============================================================================
744	# Category: plugins — editor/tmux/pre-commit/tldr/gh plugin upgrades
745	# ============================================================================
746	cat_plugins() {

748	  local ran_any=0

772	    claude_hud_installed=1

777	    info "Refreshing claude-hud plugin"
778	    _run python3 "$claude_hud_helper" --only-if-installed || any_fail=1
779	    ran_any=1
780	  fi
781	
782	  # pre-commit autoupdate — only when we're in the dotfiles repo itself
783	  if command -v pre-commit >/dev/null 2>&1 \
784	    && [[ -f "$_REPO_ROOT/.pre-commit-config.yaml" ]]; then
785	    info "Running pre-commit autoupdate on the dotfiles repo"
786	    (cd "$_REPO_ROOT" && _run pre-commit autoupdate) || any_fail=1
787	    ran_any=1
788	  fi
789	
790	  # tldr cache
791	  if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
792	    info "Updating tldr cache"
793	    _run tldr --update || any_fail=1
794	    ran_any=1
795	  fi
796	
797	  # gh extensions
798	  if command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
799	    info "Upgrading gh extensions"
800	    _run gh extension upgrade --all || any_fail=1
801	    ran_any=1
802	  fi
803	
804	  if [[ "$ran_any" -eq 0 ]]; then
805	    warn "no plugin managers detected — skipping"
806	    return $SKIP_RC
807	  fi
808	  return "$any_fail"
809	}

811	# ============================================================================
812	# Main: dispatch selected categories in defined order
813	# ============================================================================
814	hr
815	if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
816	  info "upgrade_tools.sh — categories: ${SELECTED[*]} (dry-run)"
817	else
818	  info "upgrade_tools.sh — categories: ${SELECTED[*]}"
819	fi
820	if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
821	  warn "DRY-RUN MODE — commands are printed, not executed"
822	fi
823	
824	# Run in the canonical ALL_CATEGORIES order (regardless of CLI arg order).
825	for cat in "${ALL_CATEGORIES[@]}"; do
826	  for sel in "${SELECTED[@]}"; do
827	    if [[ "$cat" == "$sel" ]]; then
828	      case "$cat" in
829	        externals) run_category externals cat_externals ;;
830	        brew) run_category brew cat_brew ;;
831	        mise) run_category mise cat_mise ;;
832	        uv) run_category uv cat_uv ;;
833	        npm) run_category npm cat_npm ;;
834	        cargo) run_category cargo cat_cargo ;;
835	        dotnet) run_category dotnet cat_dotnet ;;
836	        gem) run_category gem cat_gem ;;
837	        flatpak) run_category flatpak cat_flatpak ;;
838	        warp) run_category warp cat_warp ;;
839	        agents) run_category agents cat_agents ;;
840	        plugins) run_category plugins cat_plugins ;;
841	      esac
842	      break
843	    fi
844	  done
845	done
846	
847	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
848	# Summary
849	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
850	hr
851	info "Upgrade Summary"
852	if [[ ${#SUCCESS_CATS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
853	  success "OK:      ${SUCCESS_CATS[*]}"
854	fi
855	if [[ ${#SKIP_CATS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
856	  warn "SKIPPED: ${SKIP_CATS[*]} (prerequisite missing)"
857	fi
858	if [[ ${#FAIL_CATS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
859	  error "FAILED:  ${FAIL_CATS[*]}"
860	  for c in "${FAIL_CATS[@]}"; do
861	    error "   - ${c}: ${FAIL_REASONS[$c]:-unknown}"
862	  done
863	  exit 1
864	fi
865	exit 0

22	  tags: [sudo]

24	    name:
25	      - git

28	      - wget
29	      - ripgrep

31	      - jq
32	      - tree
33	      - build-essential
34	    state: present

36	    cache_valid_time: 3600
37	
38	- name: Create fd symlink on Debian/Ubuntu
39	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
40	  become: true
41	  tags: [sudo]
42	  ansible.builtin.file:
43	    src: /usr/bin/fdfind
44	    dest: /usr/bin/fd
45	    state: link
46	  ignore_errors: true
47	
48	# RedHat (CentOS/Rocky/Alma) base packages. ripgrep + fd skipped here:
49	# they're EPEL-only on CentOS 7 and the GitHub-release fallback below
50	# handles them more reliably (musl tarballs ignore glibc 2.17). Skipped
51	# entirely on noRoot (tags: [sudo] → --skip-tags sudo).
52	#
53	# Why `command: yum install` instead of `ansible.builtin.yum:`?
54	# ansible-core 2.18+ collapsed the yum module into a wrapper that
55	# routes through the dnf module backend. On CentOS 7 there is no `dnf`
56	# binary, so `ansible.builtin.yum:` aborts with
57	# `Could not detect which major revision of dnf is in use`. Rocky/Alma 8+
58	# do ship dnf, but using yum CLI works on both — see
59	# pitfalls/centos7-ansible-yum-dnf-backend.md.
60	- name: Install base packages (RedHat/CentOS) — yum CLI for CentOS 7 + Rocky/Alma compat
61	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
62	  become: true
63	  tags: [sudo]
64	  # Why `${missing[*]:-}` instead of `${#missing[@]}`?
65	  # Jinja2 templating in ansible reads `${#...}` as a comment block
66	  # (`{# ... #}` in Jinja syntax) and aborts with "unbalanced jinja2 block".
67	  # `${missing[*]:-}` expands to space-joined elements (empty when unset)
68	  # so `[ -z ... ]` cleanly tests "any missing packages" without `{#`.
69	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
70	    set -e
71	    missing=()
72	    for p in git git-lfs curl wget jq tree gcc gcc-c++ make; do
73	      rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
74	    done
75	    if [ -z "${missing[*]:-}" ]; then
76	      echo "ALL_INSTALLED"
77	      exit 0
78	    fi
79	    yum install -y "${missing[@]}"
80	  args:

49	# Override locale to a safe default so ansible can start even before locale
50	# packages are installed. Prefer C.UTF-8 (universal since glibc 2.35) but
51	# fall back to en_US.UTF-8 on CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17) where C.UTF-8 is
52	# missing and `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` triggers
53	# `Ansible could not initialize the preferred locale: unsupported locale
54	# setting`. Fall through silently if neither is available — the parent
55	# shell's LANG/LC_ALL (e.g. set via ENV in Dockerfile.centos7) wins.
56	if locale -a 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE '^C\.utf-?8$'; then
57	    export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
58	    export LANG=C.UTF-8
59	elif locale -a 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE '^en_US\.utf-?8$'; then
60	    export LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8
61	    export LANG=en_US.UTF-8
62	fi

85	# Linuxbrew — guard on the binary, not the dir. A failed Homebrew install
86	# leaves the /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/ tree behind (sudo'd by the
87	# installer) without the brew binary, and `eval "$(.../bin/brew shellenv)"`
88	# would then noisy-fail on every chezmoi apply. See
89	# pitfalls/bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md → CentOS 7 brew note.
90	if [[ -x /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew ]]; then
91	    eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
92	elif [[ -x "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" ]]; then

127	# === Target Python interpreter override (CentOS 7 + similar) ===
128	#
129	# ansible-core 2.18+ modules wrap themselves in `from __future__ import
130	# annotations` (Py3.7+ syntax). When ansible runs against a target whose
131	# auto-discovered `/usr/bin/python3` is older (CentOS 7 ships 3.6.8),
132	# every task fails at the Gathering Facts stage with:
133	#   SyntaxError: future feature annotations is not defined
134	#
135	# Detect the auto-discovered python's version; if < 3.7, fall back to
136	# uv's managed python (already pulled into ~/.local/share/uv/python/...
137	# by `uv tool install ansible-core` in bootstrap) and pass it via
138	# -e ansible_python_interpreter. This is forward-compatible: on Rocky 9
139	# (Py 3.9+) the override is unnecessary and the if-branch is skipped.
140	#
141	# See pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md → "controller Python pin" for the
142	# matching controller-side fix; this is the target-side companion.
143	ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP=""
144	detect_target_python() {
145	    local sys_py="${1:-/usr/bin/python3}"
146	    if ! [[ -x "$sys_py" ]]; then
147	        return 1
148	    fi
149	    local sys_ver
150	    sys_ver="$("$sys_py" -c 'import sys; print(f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}")' 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
151	    # Pure-bash version comparison: Python is fine if >= 3.7
152	    awk -v v="$sys_ver" 'BEGIN { split(v, a, "."); exit !(a[1]>3 || (a[1]==3 && a[2]>=7)) }'
153	}
154	if ! detect_target_python; then
155	    # Find a Python 3.10+ via uv (controller used --python 3.13 by bootstrap).
156	    # Search uv's managed python dir + falls back to `uv python find` if uv is on PATH.
157	    UV_PY_CANDIDATE=""
158	    for cand in "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.13.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
159	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
160	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.11.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
161	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.10.*-linux-*/bin/python3; do
162	        if [[ -x "$cand" ]]; then
163	            UV_PY_CANDIDATE="$cand"
164	            break
165	        fi
166	    done
167	    if [[ -z "$UV_PY_CANDIDATE" ]] && command -v uv &> /dev/null; then
168	        UV_PY_CANDIDATE="$(uv python find 3.13 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.12 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.11 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.10 2>/dev/null)"
169	    fi
170	    if [[ -n "$UV_PY_CANDIDATE" && -x "$UV_PY_CANDIDATE" ]]; then
171	        ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP="$UV_PY_CANDIDATE"
172	        info "System python3 < 3.7; using uv-managed Python at $ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP"
173	    else
174	        warn "System python3 < 3.7 and no uv-managed python found; ansible Gathering Facts may fail"
175	        warn "Manual fallback: \`uv python install 3.13 && chezmoi apply\`"
176	    fi
177	fi

288	# === Handle sudo (delegated to scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) ==================
289	# The helper (sudo_session_init) is idempotent: if bootstrap already prompted
290	# the user and spawned the watchdog, this call just re-exports the env vars.
291	# If ansible is run standalone (bypassing bootstrap), it prompts here instead.
292	#
293	# After init we classify via sudo_session_skip_reason:
294	#   "cached"           -> pass $CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE to ansible via -e @
295	#   "passwordless"     -> no become password needed
296	#   "non-interactive"  -> caller-specific fallback (below)
297	# Importantly we DO NOT run `sudo -k` here anymore — doing so would throw away
298	# the bootstrap-era cache and force a second prompt for the ansible phase.
299	BECOME_FLAGS=""
300	{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
301	{{ $noRoot := false }}{{ if hasKey . "noRoot" }}{{ $noRoot = .noRoot }}{{ end -}}
302	{{ if $noRoot -}}
303	info "noRoot mode enabled on macOS - skipping input_method (requires sudo for pkg installers)"
304	TAGS="${TAGS//,input_method/}"
305	{{ else -}}
306	# input_method role uses Homebrew cask pkg installers (Squirrel) which invoke
307	# `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` internally. Pre-warm the sudo timestamp via the
308	# shared helper so the non-TTY child process finds a live ticket.
309	if [[ "$NEED_SUDO" == "1" ]]; then
310	    if sudo_session_init "ansible"; then
311	        case "$(sudo_session_skip_reason)" in
312	            cached)
313	                # Refresh the current TTY's sudo timestamp so the cask child
314	                # `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` finds a live ticket (it does not
315	                # accept a piped password). The watchdog keeps it warm every 50s.
316	                sudo_session_warm_cache || warn "sudo_session_warm_cache failed; pkg casks may still prompt"
317	                ;;
318	            passwordless)
319	                info "Passwordless sudo detected"
320	                ;;
321	            non-interactive | "")
322	                warn "Non-interactive mode without passwordless sudo - pkg-based casks may be skipped"
323	                ;;
324	        esac
325	    else
326	        warn "Sudo session could not be established - pkg-based casks may be skipped"
327	    fi
328	fi
329	{{ end -}}
330	{{ else -}}
331	{{ $noRoot := false }}{{ if hasKey . "noRoot" }}{{ $noRoot = .noRoot }}{{ end -}}
332	{{ if $noRoot -}}
333	# noRoot mode: skip all sudo-requiring tasks, user-level fallbacks will install tools
334	info "noRoot mode enabled - installing user-level tools to ~/.local/bin"
335	info ""
336	info "The following tools will be installed without sudo:"
337	info "  neovim, fzf, lazygit, gh, diffnav, ripgrep, fd, jq, just, bat, eza, delta,"
338	info "  yazi, zellij, btop, gitleaks, zoxide, tldr, pre-commit, thefuck,"
339	info "  duckdb, rclone, litellm, llmfit, models"
340	info ""
341	info "The following tools require sudo (ask your administrator):"
342	info "  git, curl, wget, zsh, tmux, htop, direnv, build-essential, docker, ollama"
343	info ""
344	info "Suggested command for your administrator:"
345	info "  sudo apt install git curl wget zsh tmux htop direnv build-essential tree"
346	info ""
347	BECOME_FLAGS="--skip-tags sudo"
348	# Ruby can't compile without libffi-dev (requires sudo on Ubuntu)
349	TAGS="${TAGS//,ruby_gem_tools/}"
350	# gui_apps_linux: --skip-tags sudo already skips system apt/deb installers;
351	# this extra-var flips the user-level AppImageLauncher Lite path on so noRoot
352	# users still get AppImage desktop integration.
353	if [[ "$TAGS" == *gui_apps* ]]; then
354	    if [[ -z "$EXTRA_VARS" ]]; then
355	        EXTRA_VARS="gui_apps_linux_no_root=true"
356	    else
357	        EXTRA_VARS="$EXTRA_VARS gui_apps_linux_no_root=true"
358	    fi
359	fi
360	{{ if $installLlmTools -}}
361	if [[ -z "$EXTRA_VARS" ]]; then
362	    EXTRA_VARS="llm_tools_no_root=true"
363	else
364	    EXTRA_VARS="$EXTRA_VARS llm_tools_no_root=true"
365	fi
366	{{ end -}}
367	{{ else -}}
368	# Non-noRoot Linux: the shared helper gives us one of three outcomes.
369	if ! sudo_session_init "ansible"; then
370	    warn "Non-interactive mode without passwordless sudo and no /dev/tty access"
371	    warn "Skipping ansible run. To complete setup, run manually:"
372	    warn ""
373	    if [[ -n "$ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP" ]]; then
374	        warn "  cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook -i inventories/localhost.ini \\"
375	        warn "    $PLAYBOOK \\"
376	        warn "    --tags '$TAGS' --ask-become-pass \\"
377	        warn "    -e ansible_python_interpreter=$ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP"
378	    else
379	        warn "  cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook -i inventories/localhost.ini \\"
380	        warn "    $PLAYBOOK \\"
381	        warn "    --tags '$TAGS' --ask-become-pass"
382	    fi
383	    warn ""
384	    warn "Or grant passwordless sudo:"
385	    warn "  echo '$USER ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/$USER"
386	    exit 0
387	fi
388	case "$(sudo_session_skip_reason)" in
389	    cached)
390	        info "Sudo session active (password cached; ansible becomes via -e @ans-become.yml)"
391	        BECOME_FLAGS="-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE"
392	        ;;
393	    passwordless)
394	        info "Passwordless sudo detected"
395	        BECOME_FLAGS=""
396	        ;;
397	    non-interactive | "")
398	        # Shouldn't hit this after a successful sudo_session_init, but keep
399	        # the manual-command fallback in case probes contradict each other.
400	        warn "Sudo state inconsistent after session init; falling back to manual instructions"
401	        warn "  cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook -i inventories/localhost.ini \\"
402	        warn "    $PLAYBOOK \\"
403	        warn "    --tags '$TAGS' --ask-become-pass"
404	        exit 0
405	        ;;
406	esac
407	{{ end -}}
408	{{ end -}}

410	info "Profile: {{ .profile }}"
411	info "Re-running ansible with tags: $TAGS"
412	EXTRA_VARS_ARGS=()
413	[[ -n "$EXTRA_VARS" ]] && EXTRA_VARS_ARGS=(--extra-vars "$EXTRA_VARS")
414	# When the system Python is too old for ansible-core 2.18+ modules
415	# (CentOS 7 etc.), prepend an explicit ansible_python_interpreter override
416	# so all role tasks use uv's managed Python instead of /usr/bin/python3.
417	if [[ -n "$ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP" ]]; then
418	    EXTRA_VARS_ARGS+=(--extra-vars "ansible_python_interpreter=$ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP")
419	fi

421	{{ $allowPartialFailure := false }}{{ if hasKey . "allowPartialFailure" }}{{ $allowPartialFailure = .allowPartialFailure }}{{ end -}}
422	{{ if $allowPartialFailure -}}
423	# Best-effort mode: run each tag separately so one failure doesn't block others
424	info "allowPartialFailure=true: running each tag independently"
425	FAILED_TAGS=()
426	IFS=',' read -ra TAG_ARRAY <<< "$TAGS"
427	for tag in "${TAG_ARRAY[@]}"; do
428	    info "────── Running tag: $tag ──────"
429	    ansible-playbook -i "$INVENTORY" "$PLAYBOOK" --tags "$tag" $BECOME_FLAGS "${EXTRA_VARS_ARGS[@]}" || {
430	        warn "Tag '$tag' had failures (continuing in best-effort mode)"
431	        FAILED_TAGS+=("$tag")
432	    }
433	done
434	if [[ ${#FAILED_TAGS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
435	    warn "────── Summary ──────"
436	    warn "The following tags had failures: ${FAILED_TAGS[*]}"
437	    warn "Retry manually:"
438	    warn "  cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook -i inventories/localhost.ini $PLAYBOOK --tags '$(IFS=,; echo "${FAILED_TAGS[*]}")' $BECOME_FLAGS ${EXTRA_VARS_ARGS[*]}"
439	    success "Ansible roles partially updated (${#FAILED_TAGS[@]} tag(s) failed)."
440	else
441	    success "Ansible roles updated!"
442	fi
443	{{ else -}}
444	ansible-playbook -i "$INVENTORY" "$PLAYBOOK" --tags "$TAGS" $BECOME_FLAGS "${EXTRA_VARS_ARGS[@]}"
445	success "Ansible roles updated!"
446	{{ end -}}
447

1	---
2	# Base role - essential tools across platforms
3	
4	- name: Install base packages (macOS)
5	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
6	  community.general.homebrew:
7	    name:
8	      - git
9	      - git-lfs
10	      - curl
11	      - wget
12	      - ripgrep
13	      - fd
14	      - jq
15	      - tree
16	      - just
17	    state: present
18	
19	- name: Install base packages (Debian/Ubuntu)
20	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
21	  become: true
22	  tags: [sudo]
23	  ansible.builtin.apt:
24	    name:
25	      - git
26	      - git-lfs
27	      - curl
28	      - wget
29	      - ripgrep
30	      - fd-find
31	      - jq
32	      - tree
33	      - build-essential
34	    state: present
35	    update_cache: true
36	    cache_valid_time: 3600
37	
38	- name: Create fd symlink on Debian/Ubuntu
39	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
40	  become: true
41	  tags: [sudo]
42	  ansible.builtin.file:
43	    src: /usr/bin/fdfind
44	    dest: /usr/bin/fd
45	    state: link
46	  ignore_errors: true
47	
48	# RedHat (CentOS/Rocky/Alma) base packages. ripgrep + fd skipped here:
49	# they're EPEL-only on CentOS 7 and the GitHub-release fallback below
50	# handles them more reliably (musl tarballs ignore glibc 2.17). Skipped
51	# entirely on noRoot (tags: [sudo] → --skip-tags sudo).
52	#
53	# Why `command: yum install` instead of `ansible.builtin.yum:`?
54	# ansible-core 2.18+ collapsed the yum module into a wrapper that
55	# routes through the dnf module backend. On CentOS 7 there is no `dnf`
56	# binary, so `ansible.builtin.yum:` aborts with
57	# `Could not detect which major revision of dnf is in use`. Rocky/Alma 8+
58	# do ship dnf, but using yum CLI works on both — see
59	# pitfalls/centos7-ansible-yum-dnf-backend.md.
60	- name: Install base packages (RedHat/CentOS) — yum CLI for CentOS 7 + Rocky/Alma compat
61	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
62	  become: true
63	  tags: [sudo]
64	  # Why `${missing[*]:-}` instead of `${#missing[@]}`?
65	  # Jinja2 templating in ansible reads `${#...}` as a comment block
66	  # (`{# ... #}` in Jinja syntax) and aborts with "unbalanced jinja2 block".
67	  # `${missing[*]:-}` expands to space-joined elements (empty when unset)
68	  # so `[ -z ... ]` cleanly tests "any missing packages" without `{#`.
69	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
70	    set -e
71	    missing=()
72	    for p in git git-lfs curl wget jq tree gcc gcc-c++ make; do
73	      rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
74	    done
75	    if [ -z "${missing[*]:-}" ]; then
76	      echo "ALL_INSTALLED"
77	      exit 0
78	    fi
79	    yum install -y "${missing[@]}"
80	  args:
81	    executable: /bin/bash
82	  register: base_yum_result
83	  changed_when: "'ALL_INSTALLED' not in base_yum_result.stdout"
84	  ignore_errors: true
85	
86	# --- ripgrep (user-level fallback) ---
87	- name: Re-check if ripgrep is installed
88	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
89	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v rg
90	  register: rg_recheck
91	  changed_when: false
92	  failed_when: false
93	
94	- name: Install ripgrep from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
95	  when:
96	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
97	    - rg_recheck.rc != 0
98	  block:
99	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (ripgrep)
100	      ansible.builtin.file:
101	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
102	        state: directory
103	        mode: '0755'
104	
105	    - name: Set ripgrep release target
106	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
107	        rg_target: >-
108	          {{
109	            target_architecture ~ '-unknown-linux-musl'
110	            if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
111	            else 'arm-unknown-linux-gnueabihf'
112	            if target_architecture in ['armv7l', 'armhf']
113	            else ''
114	          }}
115	
116	    - name: Get latest ripgrep release
117	      when: rg_target | trim != ''
118	      ansible.builtin.uri:
119	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases/latest
120	        return_content: true
121	      register: rg_release
122	
123	    - name: Download ripgrep binary
124	      when: rg_target | trim != ''
125	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
126	        url: "https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases/download/{{ rg_release.json.tag_name }}/ripgrep-{{ rg_release.json.tag_name }}-{{ rg_target }}.tar.gz"
127	        dest: /tmp/ripgrep.tar.gz
128	        mode: '0644'
129	        timeout: 120
130	      retries: 3
131	      delay: 5
132	
133	    - name: Extract ripgrep
134	      when: rg_target | trim != ''
135	      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
136	        src: /tmp/ripgrep.tar.gz
137	        dest: /tmp
138	        remote_src: true
139	
140	    - name: Install ripgrep to ~/.local/bin
141	      when: rg_target | trim != ''
142	      ansible.builtin.copy:
143	        src: "/tmp/ripgrep-{{ rg_release.json.tag_name }}-{{ rg_target }}/rg"
144	        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/rg"
145	        mode: '0755'
146	        remote_src: true

1	---
2	# Security tools role - pre-commit and gitleaks for secret scanning
3	#
4	# pre-commit is installed via `uv tool install --python 3.13` on BOTH macOS and
5	# Linux so the Python bootstrap is identical across machines. This avoids the
6	# macOS Homebrew `python@3.14` pyexpat / libexpat ABI mismatch that breaks
7	# virtualenv creation for hook repos (symptom:
8	# `Symbol not found: _XML_SetAllocTrackerActivationThreshold`). See
9	# `docs/tools/pre-commit.md` for the full rationale.
10	#
11	# `uv` itself is installed by `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` before any
12	# ansible role runs, so we can depend on it here unconditionally.
13	
14	- name: Check uv is available (prereq for pre-commit install)
15	  ansible.builtin.command: uv --version

1	---
2	# Python CLI tools via uv
3	# uv is bootstrapped before ansible runs
4	
5	# Detect whether the system has a modern-enough GCC for numpy 2.x / pandas
6	# 3.x / pyarrow source builds. Modern wheel ecosystem dropped manylinux_2_17
7	# (CentOS 7 baseline) so older glibc hosts fall back to compiling these from
8	# source — and the build now requires GCC >= 9.3 (numpy meson build asserts).
9	# CentOS 7 ships gcc 4.8.5; the tools tagged `needs_modern_gcc: true` get
10	# skipped there. See pitfalls/centos7-numpy-pandas-source-build.md.
11	- name: Detect host C compiler (gcc) version
12	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
13	    set -e
14	    if command -v gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
15	      gcc -dumpversion 2>/dev/null | head -1
16	    else
17	      echo "0"
18	    fi
19	  args:
20	    executable: /bin/bash
21	  register: gcc_version_probe
22	  changed_when: false
23	  failed_when: false
24	
25	- name: Set fact gcc_too_old (true when major < 9)
26	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
27	    gcc_too_old: >-
28	      {{ ((gcc_version_probe.stdout | trim).split('.')[0] | int) < 9 }}
29	
30	- name: Install Python CLI tools via uv
31	  ansible.builtin.command: >-
32	    uv tool install {{ item.name }}
33	    {% if item.python is defined %}--python {{ item.python }} {% endif %}
34	    {% if item.with is defined %}{% for dep in item.with %}--with {{ dep }} {% endfor %}{% endif %}
35	  register: python_uv_tool_install
36	  until: python_uv_tool_install is succeeded
37	  retries: 3
38	  delay: 5
39	  args:
40	    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.binary }}"
41	  environment:
42	    UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT: "120"
43	    UV_HTTP_RETRIES: "5"
44	  # Skip tools that pull numpy 2.x / pandas 3.x source-build chain when
45	  # the host's GCC can't compile them (e.g. CentOS 7 — gcc 4.8.5).
46	  when: not (item.needs_modern_gcc | default(false) and gcc_too_old)
47	  loop: "{{ python_uv_tools }}"
48	  loop_control:
49	    label: "{{ item.name }}{% if item.needs_modern_gcc | default(false) and gcc_too_old %} [SKIPPED: needs gcc >= 9]{% endif %}"

### 4. KEY MULTI-OS INSTALLATION PATTERNS

#### **Pattern A: Homebrew on macOS, apt on Linux**

Example from `base` role:
```yaml
# macOS - Homebrew
- name: Install base packages (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name: [git, curl, wget, ripgrep, fd, jq, tree, just]

# Linux - apt
- name: Install base packages (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: [git, curl, wget, ripgrep, fd-find, jq, tree, build-essential]
    update_cache: true
    cache_valid_time: 3600

# Note: fd-find → symlink as fd on Debian/Ubuntu
- name: Create fd symlink on Debian/Ubuntu
  ansible.builtin.file:
    src: /usr/bin/fdfind
    dest: /usr/bin/fd
    state: link
```

#### **Pattern B: GitHub Release Download with Architecture Mapping**

Used by ~20 roles (devtools, networking_tools, security_tools, iac_tools, etc.)

Example from `devtools` (gh installation):
```yaml
- name: Check if gh is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  command: gh --version
  register: gh_check

- name: Set gh release architecture
  set_fact:
    gh_release_arch: >-
      {{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
         else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
         else '' }}

# System-level install with sudo
- name: Install gh from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - gh_check.rc != 0
    - gh_release_arch != ''
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  block:
    - name: Get latest gh release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/releases/latest
      register: gh_release
    
    - name: Download gh .deb package
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/{{ gh_release.json.tag_name }}/gh_{{ ... }}_linux_{{ gh_release_arch }}.deb"
        dest: /tmp/gh.deb
    
    - name: Install gh .deb
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        deb: /tmp/gh.deb

# User-level fallback (no sudo)
- name: Install gh from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - gh_recheck.rc != 0
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
    
    - name: Download & extract gh tarball
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "...gh_{{ ... }}_linux_{{ gh_release_arch }}.tar.gz"
        dest: /tmp/gh.tar.gz
    
    - name: Extract & install
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        tar -xzf /tmp/gh.tar.gz -C /tmp/gh-extract
        gh_bin="$(find /tmp/gh-extract -path '*/bin/gh' | head -n1)"
        install -m 0755 "$gh_bin" "$HOME/.local/bin/gh"
```

**Key Features:**
- System-level install with `become: true` (via apt/deb)
- Fallback to user-level (`~/.local/bin`) if sudo fails
- Retries: 3 attempts with 5s delay for network resilience
- Architecture mapping: x86_64/amd64 → amd64, aarch64/arm64 → arm64
- Cleanup: removes temp files in rescue block

#### **Pattern C: Language-Specific Package Managers (uv, cargo, gem)**

Example from `security_tools` (pre-commit via uv):
```yaml
- name: Install pre-commit via uv (pinned Python 3.13, all OSes)
  ansible.builtin.command: uv tool install --force pre-commit --python 3.13
  changed_when: "'already installed' not in output"
```

Example from `python_uv_tools`:
```yaml
- name: Install Python CLI tools via uv
  command: >-
    uv tool install {{ item.name }}
    {% if item.python %}--python {{ item.python }}{% endif %}
    {% if item.with %}{% for dep in item.with %}--with {{ dep }}{% endfor %}{% endif %}
  args:
    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.binary }}"
  environment:
    UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT: "120"
    UV_HTTP_RETRIES: "5"
  when: not (item.needs_modern_gcc and gcc_too_old)
  loop: "{{ python_uv_tools }}"
```

#### **Pattern D: Conditional Installation with Defaults**

Example from `iac_tools`:
```yaml
# defaults/main.yml
iac_install_azure_cli: true
iac_install_terraform: true
iac_install_opentofu: true

# tasks/main.yml
- name: Install Azure CLI (macOS)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
    - iac_install_azure_cli
  block:
    - name: Install azure-cli via Homebrew
      community.general.homebrew:
        name: azure-cli
      register: az_brew_install
      until: az_brew_install is succeeded
      retries: 3
      delay: 20
  rescue:
    - name: Warn Azure CLI failed
      debug:
        msg: "Azure CLI installation failed — skipping."
```

#### **Pattern E: RedHat/CentOS Support with yum CLI**

Used in `base`, `networking_tools`, `iac_tools` roles:
```yaml
- name: Install base packages (RedHat/CentOS) — yum CLI for CentOS 7 compat
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
  become: true
  shell: |
    set -e
    missing=()
    for p in git curl wget jq tree gcc; do
      rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
    done
    if [ -z "${missing[*]:-}" ]; then
      echo "ALL_INSTALLED"
      exit 0
    fi
    yum install -y "${missing[@]}"
  changed_when: "'ALL_INSTALLED' not in output"
```

**Why yum CLI instead of ansible.builtin.yum?**
- ansible-core 2.18+ routes yum through dnf backend
- CentOS 7 has no dnf binary → breaks
- `yum` CLI works on CentOS 7, Rocky 8+, Alma 8+ (see `pitfalls/centos7-ansible-yum-dnf-backend.md`)

#### **Pattern F: CentOS 7 GCC Version Detection**

From `python_uv_tools`:
```yaml
- name: Detect host C compiler (gcc) version
  shell: gcc -dumpversion 2>/dev/null | head -1 || echo "0"
  register: gcc_version_probe

- name: Set fact gcc_too_old
  set_fact:
    gcc_too_old: "{{ ((gcc_version_probe.stdout | trim).split('.')[0] | int) < 9 }}"

# Skip numpy 2.x / pandas 3.x builds on CentOS 7 (gcc 4.8.5)
when: not (item.needs_modern_gcc and gcc_too_old)
```

### 5. CHEZMOI INTEGRATION & BREWFILE EXECUTION

**Location:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`

**When it runs:**
- Triggered when any Brewfile changes (chezmoi run_onchange)
- Only if `installBrewApps: true` or macOS + `installAiDesktopApps: true`

**How it works:**
```bash
# Detects Homebrew path (Intel vs Apple Silicon, macOS vs Linuxbrew)
if [[ -f /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
fi

# Runs shared Brewfile first (installs mas, taps)
run_bundle_with_retry "$BREWFILE_DIR/Brewfile" "shared packages"

# Runs platform-specific file
if [[ eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" ]]; then
    run_bundle_with_retry "$BREWFILE_DIR/Brewfile.darwin" "macOS packages"
else
    run_bundle_with_retry "$BREWFILE_DIR/Brewfile.linux" "Linux packages"
fi

# Retries with BUNDLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2 (default)
run_bundle_with_retry() {
    local file="$1"
    for attempt in 1 .. N; do
        if brew bundle --file="$file" --no-upgrade; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
}
```

**Architecture Support:**
- macOS: Detects `/opt/homebrew` (Apple Silicon) vs `/usr/local` (Intel)
- Linux: Detects `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew` vs `$HOME/.linuxbrew`
- Sudo handling: Pre-authenticates for macOS cask installers (e.g., google-drive, ollama-app)

### 10. ERROR HANDLING & RESILIENCE

**Patterns used:**

1. **Retries with exponential backoff:**
   ```yaml
   retries: 3
   delay: 5
   until: result is succeeded
   ```

2. **Network timeout protection:**
   ```yaml
   environment:
     UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT: "120"
     UV_HTTP_RETRIES: "5"
   timeout: 120
   ```

3. **Block + rescue for graceful degradation:**
   ```yaml
   block:
     - name: System-level install
   rescue:
     - name: Warn and clean up
       debug: msg "Installation failed — skipping"
     - name: Clean temp files
   ```

4. **Ignore errors on optional installs:**
   ```yaml
   ignore_errors: true  # (for non-critical tools)
   ```

5. **Brew bundle retry with partial success:**
   ```bash
   # Retries up to N times; subsequent runs only retry failed items
   brew bundle --no-upgrade
   ```

# 是否安裝影音/媒體 CLI 工具 (ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips)
# ffmpeg 也是 vhs 的 runtime 依賴；裝了影音包之後 vhs 才能真正錄製。詳見 docs/tools/ffmpeg.md
installMediaTools = {{ promptBoolOnce . "installMediaTools" "Install media/AV CLI tools (ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips)" false }}
# 是否安裝 .NET SDK (via mise) 與 .NET global tools (azure-cost-cli, 等)
installDotnetTools = {{ promptBoolOnce . "installDotnetTools" "Install .NET SDK via mise and dotnet global tools (azure-cost-cli, etc.)" false }}
# 沒有 sudo/root 權限，只安裝 user-level 工具 (mise, cargo, gem, uv, npm)
noRoot = {{ promptBoolOnce . "noRoot" "No sudo/root access - skip all system package installations" false }}
# 在 chezmoi apply 之前備份現有的 dotfiles。
# smart = 只備份 chezmoi 將要覆蓋/刪除的檔案（用 `chezmoi status` 偵測）
# full  = 備份固定 allowlist（onboard 第一次最保險）
# off   = 完全跳過（CI / Docker / 一次性環境用）
backupMode = {{ promptChoiceOnce . "backupMode" "Backup mode for existing dotfiles (smart|full|off)" (list "smart" "full" "off") "smart" | quote }}
# 允許 Ansible 部分失敗（逐 tag 執行，單一 role 失敗不影響其餘）
allowPartialFailure = {{ promptBoolOnce . "allowPartialFailure" "Allow partial Ansible failures (continue installing other tools if one role fails)" false }}
# SSH login banner (~/.zlogin) 樣式 — 詳見 docs/zsh/motd.md
#   - figlet:         單行 figlet hostname + metadata（~6 行，~5ms，預設）
#   - fastfetch-slim: figlet hostname + fastfetch 精簡版（~10 行，~80ms）
#   - fastfetch-full: fastfetch 完整輸出含 distro logo（~22 行，~150ms）
# Runtime override: 在 ~/.zshrc.adhoc 設 MOTD_STYLE=... 可即時切換無需 chezmoi init --force
motdStyle = {{ promptChoiceOnce . "motdStyle" "SSH login banner style (figlet|fastfetch-slim|fastfetch-full)" (list "figlet" "fastfetch-slim" "fastfetch-full") "figlet" | quote }}
# Primary interactive shell — decides which shell `chsh` switches to as the
# login shell. Both ~/.zshrc and ~/.bashrc are deployed regardless (so the
# other shell still works ad-hoc); only the login-shell switch is gated.
# Bash side ships with oh-my-bash + ble.sh for a UX close to zsh; on macOS
# the bash role also brew-installs bash 5.x (system bash 3.2 is too old for
# OMB plugins) when bash is selected. See docs/shells/bash.md.
primaryShell = {{ promptChoiceOnce . "primaryShell" "Primary interactive shell (zsh|bash)" (list "zsh" "bash") "zsh" | quote }}

# https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/use-scripts-to-perform-actions/#dont-show-scripts-that-would-run-in-chezmoi-diffchezmoi-status
[diff]
    exclude = ["scripts"]
{{- if lookPath "delta" }}
    # Side-by-side diff: left = current (before apply), right = target (after apply)
    pager = "delta --side-by-side --line-numbers --navigate --paging=always --file-style=yellow --file-decoration-style='yellow ul' --hunk-header-decoration-style='blue box'"
{{- end }}
[status]
    exclude = ["scripts"]
```

---
# Networking CLI tools role
# Tools: nmap, arp-scan, mtr, iperf3, doggo, httpie, gping, trippy, bandwhich, speedtest, rustscan

# =============================================================================
# macOS - all via Homebrew
# =============================================================================

- name: Install networking tools (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - nmap
      - arp-scan
      - mtr
      - iperf3
      - doggo
      - httpie
      - gping
      - trippy
      - bandwhich
      - rustscan
    state: present

- name: Install Ookla Speedtest CLI (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  block:
    - name: Check if teamookla/speedtest tap is present
      ansible.builtin.command: brew tap
      register: speedtest_taps
      changed_when: false

    - name: Tap teamookla/speedtest
      ansible.builtin.command: brew tap teamookla/speedtest
      when: "'teamookla/speedtest' not in speedtest_taps.stdout_lines"

    - name: Install speedtest
      community.general.homebrew:
        name: speedtest
        state: present

# =============================================================================
# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)
# =============================================================================

# --- system-level packages (apt) ---
- name: Install networking tools from apt (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - nmap
      - arp-scan
      - mtr
      - iperf3
      - httpie
      - tcpdump
    state: present

# --- system-level packages (yum/CentOS 7+) ---
# yum CLI for CentOS 7 compat — see pitfalls/centos7-ansible-yum-dnf-backend.md
- name: Install networking tools from yum (RedHat/CentOS) — yum CLI for CentOS 7 + Rocky/Alma compat
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -e
    missing=()
    for p in nmap arp-scan mtr iperf3 tcpdump; do
      rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$p")
    done
    # NOTE: httpie is in EPEL on CentOS 7 and pip-installed via uv elsewhere
    # if missing, so we skip it here to avoid hard-requiring EPEL.
    if [ -z "${missing[*]:-}" ]; then
      echo "ALL_INSTALLED"
      exit 0
    fi
    yum install -y "${missing[@]}"
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  register: networking_yum_result
  changed_when: "'ALL_INSTALLED' not in networking_yum_result.stdout"
  ignore_errors: true

# --- Architecture mapping for GitHub release downloads ---
- name: Set networking tools release architecture
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    net_arch_deb: >-
      {{
        'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
        else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
        else target_architecture
      }}

# --- doggo (modern DNS lookup) ---
- name: Check if doggo is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
  ansible.builtin.command: doggo --version
```

# Networking CLI Tools

Optional role (`installNetworkingTools`). Install via `chezmoi init --force` and enable the prompt.

## Tools

| Tool | Binary | Purpose | Sudo at runtime? |
|------|--------|---------|-------------------|
| [nmap](https://nmap.org/) | `nmap` | Port scanning, host discovery, OS detection, service enumeration | Some features (OS detection, SYN scan) |
| [arp-scan](https://github.com/royhills/arp-scan) | `arp-scan` | Fast Layer 2 host discovery with OUI vendor lookup | Yes (raw sockets) |
| [mtr](https://www.bitwizard.nl/mtr/) | `mtr` | Real-time combined ping + traceroute | Some modes |
| [iperf3](https://iperf.fr/) | `iperf3` | Network bandwidth/throughput testing between two hosts | No |
| [doggo](https://github.com/mr-karan/doggo) | `doggo` | Modern DNS lookup (replaces dig/nslookup), DoH/DoT/DoQ | No |
| [HTTPie](https://httpie.io/) | `http` / `https` | Modern HTTP client, nicer than curl for API testing | No |
| [gping](https://github.com/orf/gping) | `gping` | Ping with a real-time graph | No |
| [trippy](https://github.com/fujiapple852/trippy) | `trip` | Modern TUI traceroute with rich visualization | Yes (raw sockets) |
| [bandwhich](https://github.com/imsnif/bandwhich) | `bandwhich` | Terminal bandwidth utilization per process/connection | Yes (packet capture) |
| [Ookla Speedtest](https://www.speedtest.net/apps/cli) | `speedtest` | Official Ookla internet speed test | No |
| [RustScan](https://github.com/RustScan/RustScan) | `rustscan` | Fast port scanner, feeds results into nmap | No |

## Shell Aliases

Defined in `~/.config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh`:

| Alias | Command | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `ports` | `lsof -i -P -n \| grep LISTEN` | Show all listening ports |
| `myip` | `curl -s https://ifconfig.me` | Show public IP address |
| `localip` | platform-aware | Show local LAN IP address |
| `arpscan` | `sudo arp-scan -l` | Scan local network (Layer 2) |
| `pingsweep` | `nmap -sn <subnet>/24` | Ping sweep local /24 subnet (function) |
| `dns` | `doggo` | DNS lookup shortcut |
| `bw-net` | `sudo bandwhich` | Bandwidth monitor (avoids conflict with `bw` = Bitwarden) |
| `portscan` | `rustscan` | Fast port scan shortcut |

## Common Usage

### What's on my network?

```bash
# Layer 2 ARP scan (most reliable, shows MAC + vendor)
arpscan

# Ping sweep (Layer 3)
pingsweep

# Full scan with OS detection
sudo nmap -sV -O 192.168.1.0/24

# Interactive picker with open ports, MAC/vendor, hostname, latency
# (auto-detects sudo; falls back to no-sudo discovery when unavailable)
lanscan            # run a full scan into ~/.cache/tv/
tv lan-devices     # fuzzy-search devices; see docs/tools/tv.md
```

### Port scanning

```bash
# Quick port scan (rustscan is ~10x faster than nmap alone)
portscan -a 192.168.1.100

# Specific ports with nmap
nmap -p 22,80,443,8080 192.168.1.100

# Service version detection
nmap -sV -p 22,80 192.168.1.100
```

### DNS lookup

```bash
# Basic lookup
dns example.com

# Specific record type
dns example.com MX
dns example.com AAAA

# Use DNS-over-HTTPS
dns example.com --class IN --type A @https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query
```
</details></tool-use>

```md
# Plan: Add ngrok + cloudflared as managed tunnel tools

## Context

ngrok and cloudflared are both installed ad-hoc on the dev machine but not managed by dotfiles.
The user wants them integrated so they auto-install across OS/profiles, and wants a `docs/tools/tunnels.md`
covering common dev tunnel workflows (expose localhost, SSH reverse tunnels, etc.).

These are "tunnel/expose" tools, distinct from the existing diagnostic networking tools (nmap, mtr, etc.).
Adding them under a new **`installTunnelTools`** flag keeps them independently opt-in, while reusing the
existing `networking_tools` role avoids creating a one-purpose role for just two binaries.

---

## Files to Change

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` | Add `installTunnelTools` prompt (default `false`) |
| `dot_ansible/roles/networking_tools/tasks/main.yml` | Add ngrok + cloudflared tasks with `tags: [tunnel_tools]` |
| `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` | Add hash of networking_tools tasks (already present); add `tunnel_tools` tag when flag is true |
| `docs/tools/tunnels.md` | New EN doc — install, common commands, env patterns |
| `docs/tools/tunnels.zh-TW.md` | New zh-TW mirror |
| `mkdocs.yml` | Add nav entry under Tools section (alphabetical near "Tailscale") |

---

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` — new prompt

Insert after the `installNetworkingTools` line:

\```toml
# 是否安裝 tunnel 工具 (ngrok, cloudflared) — expose localhost / SSH reverse tunnel
installTunnelTools = {{ promptBoolOnce . "installTunnelTools" "Install tunnel tools (ngrok, cloudflared — expose localhost, SSH tunnels)" false }}
\```

### 2. `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` — new tag gating

The file already hashes `networking_tools/tasks/main.yml` (line 37), so changing that file
will trigger a re-run automatically. Add after the `installNetworkingTools` block (~line 244):

\```bash
{{ $installTunnelTools := false }}{{ if hasKey . "installTunnelTools" }}{{ $installTunnelTools = .installTunnelTools }}{{ end -}}
{{ if $installTunnelTools -}}
TAGS="${TAGS},tunnel_tools"
{{ end -}}
\```

Also ensure `networking_tools` role is in the playbook tag list — it already is for all profiles
(both macos.yml and linux.yml include it); the new `tunnel_tools` tag will be a sub-tag within
the same role, so no playbook changes needed.

### 3. `networking_tools/tasks/main.yml` — ngrok + cloudflared tasks

Append to the end of the file. All tasks carry `tags: [tunnel_tools]`.

**Architecture variable** (reuse existing `net_arch_deb` fact already set earlier in the role).

#### ngrok

| Platform | Method |
|----------|--------|
| macOS | `brew tap ngrok/ngrok` + `brew install ngrok` |
| Linux Debian/Ubuntu | Official apt repo: add GPG key + source list + `apt install ngrok` (system-level, sudo); fallback: download tgz to `~/.local/bin` |
| Linux RedHat/CentOS | Download tgz from GitHub releases to `~/.local/bin` (no official rpm) |

ngrok Linux tgz URL pattern: `https://bin.equinox.io/c/bNyj1mQVY4c/ngrok-v3-stable-linux-{amd64|arm64}.tgz`

#### cloudflared

| Platform | Method |
|----------|--------|
| macOS | `brew install cloudflared` |
| Linux Debian/Ubuntu | Official `.deb` from GitHub releases: `cloudflared-linux-{amd64|arm64}.deb` via `apt install deb:` |
| Linux RedHat/CentOS | Official `.rpm` from GitHub releases: `cloudflared-linux-{x86_64|aarch64}.rpm` via `rpm -i` |

Both tools follow the existing block+rescue pattern (system-level first, user-level fallback).

### 4. `docs/tools/tunnels.md` (new)

Sections:
- **Installation** — how the tools are managed (ansible flag), manual install links
- **ngrok** — expose HTTP/TCP port, auth token setup (`ngrok config add-authtoken`), custom subdomains, inspect traffic at `localhost:4040`, useful flags

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Add ngrok + cloudflared as managed tunnel tools

## Context

ngrok and cloudflared are both installed ad-hoc on the dev machine but not managed by dotfiles.
The user wants them integrated so they auto-install across OS/profiles, and wants a `docs/tools/tunnels.md`
covering common dev tunnel workflows (expose localhost, SSH reverse tunnels, etc.).

These are "tunnel/expose" tools, distinct from the existing diagnostic networking tools (nmap, mtr, etc.).
Adding them under a new **`installTunnelTools`** flag keeps them independently opt-in, while reusing the
existing `networking_tools` role avoids creating a one-purpose role for just two binaries.

---

## Files to Change

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` | Add `installTunnelTools` prompt (default `false`) |
| `dot_ansible/roles/networking_tools/tasks/main.yml` | Add ngrok + cloudflared tasks with `tags: [tunnel_tools]` |
| `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` | Add hash of networking_tools tasks (already present); add `tunnel_tools` tag when flag is true |
| `docs/tools/tunnels.md` | New EN doc — install, common commands, env patterns |
| `docs/tools/tunnels.zh-TW.md` | New zh-TW mirror |
| `mkdocs.yml` | Add nav entry under Tools section (alphabetical near "Tailscale") |

---

### 1. `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` — new prompt

Insert after the `installNetworkingTools` line:

```toml

installTunnelTools = {{ promptBoolOnce . "installTunnelTools" "Install tunnel tools (ngrok, cloudflared — expose localhost, SSH tunnels)" false }}
```

### 2. `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` — new tag gating

The file already hashes `networking_tools/tasks/main.yml` (line 37), so changing that file
will trigger a re-run automatically. Add after the `installNetworkingTools` block (~line 244):

```bash
{{ $installTunnelTools := false }}{{ if hasKey . "installTunnelTools" }}{{ $installTunnelTools = .installTunnelTools }}{{ end -}}
{{ if $installTunnelTools -}}
TAGS="${TAGS},tunnel_tools"
{{ end -}}
```

Also ensure `networking_tools` role is in the playbook tag list — it already is for all profiles
(both macos.yml and linux.yml include it); the new `tunnel_tools` tag will be a sub-tag within

**Architecture variable** (reuse existing `net_arch_deb` fact already set earlier in the role).

#### ngrok

| macOS | `brew tap ngrok/ngrok` + `brew install ngrok` |

ngrok Linux tgz URL pattern: `https://bin.equinox.io/c/bNyj1mQVY4c/ngrok-v3-stable-linux-{amd64|arm64}.tgz`

#### cloudflared

|----------|--------|
| macOS | `brew install cloudflared` |
| Linux Debian/Ubuntu | Official `.deb` from GitHub releases: `cloudflared-linux-{amd64|arm64}.deb` via `apt install deb:` |
| Linux RedHat/CentOS | Official `.rpm` from GitHub releases: `cloudflared-linux-{x86_64|aarch64}.rpm` via `rpm -i` |

Both tools follow the existing block+rescue pattern (system-level first, user-level fallback).
